_doc: The Salt Creek Hotel (#1146 the design, docs/briefs/hotel.md; #1220 steps 2-6; Sean's calls on #1215: painted clapboard in three colours, two storeys, an open railed gallery to be blown up, the cellar's secret B). Format 1 (../../experiments/building_lab/FORMAT.md) with what a big two-storey hotel needs (each marked NEW). Target sheet: experiments/building_lab/hotel/sheet/ (Sean OK 2026-11-24): build the OPEN deck, not the sheet's roofed gallery. Sizes from this spec only, never off the pictures. Written by make_spec.py. SPACE: on its north-side lot the building faces south (facing 180), so its x runs from its EAST corner westward and its z back (north) from the front wall's outer stud face; the side walls are named by what they face, 'lane' (west, the saloon lane) and 'alley' (east). THE MAIN BLOCK ONLY: the two-storey kitchen wing behind its west half (42 x 24 ft) is the next step (README).

identity.owner: the landlady, a widow in her forties: her late husband built it in 1881 on the best lot on Main Street's north side and died the next winter; she runs it with a clerk, a cook, two chambermaids, a waitress and a boy
identity.trade: the town's best hotel: eleven rooms and a suite over a lobby, a small fine bar, the ladies' parlour and a dining room laid for supper; where the railroad's men, the mine's, drummers and the Army's officers stay, and where the Baron gives his suppers
identity.means: a frame building dressed as well as money freighted on the railroad could dress it: local walls, and the millwork, plate glass, carpets, paper and brass all off the cars
identity.age_and_repair: a year old and well kept: the paint fresh, the walk swept at six, the lobby's carpet paler on the way to the desk and the stair; the gallery's deck already grey
clues: SALT CREEK HOTEL in gilt on a red board over the cornice, 1881 in the pediment
lace at every upper window: the only curtains on the street
chairs and a rocker under the gallery, a boot scraper by the main doors
the bar's own door on the lane side, the ladies' at the east
a brewery's dray at the bulkhead on the saloon lane

lot._doc: valley.json town.north 'hotel' (x 42.0-67.2, 25.2 m): the building's west wall 3 cm inside the lot's line on the saloon lane (world x 42.03), its east corner (the origin) at world x 66.414, 0.79 m short of the east lane; the front wall's face on the town's front line (z -10.05). Its floor at its walk's top (walk.h 0.75 over the ground at the walk's street edge, ValleyTown); `at`'s y the street edge's ground (the bake: -0.16 east to -0.01 west). The lot is dug level at that height under the building (valley.json's pad): the bake rises 0.5-0.6 m to the back wall, which would bury the sills.

ground._doc: the pad: level at the building's y 0

levels._doc: The floor at the walk's top (0.75: four easy steps). 13 ft 6 in floor to floor below (the lobby's height, the tall plate glass), 11 ft 6 in above to the flat roof's joists; the roof's boards at 8.70, the parapet's cornice and the name board to 9.9 (32 1/2 ft over the street, the brief's front). The cellar's floor 2.0 m under the street edge (its flags 1.92: 2.2 m clear under the girders).

frame._doc: A balloon frame (Bell 1858; Woodward 1865): 4x4 studs sill to plate through both storeys (saloon B's, under a crowd), the upper joists on a 1x6 ribbon let into them. The ground floor's 2x10 joists front to back on four lines of girders, broken over each; the upper floor's 3x14 at 12 in front to back over the 28 ft rooms (Kidder: no wood joist over 25 ft without a reason; Hatfield 1880 for the sizes), broken over the long bearing wall at 28 ft; a flat roof of 2x12 at 16 in on the plates, the bearing partitions and a ribbon on the front's studs, boarded and tinned (terne plate on boards, the period's flat roof behind a parapet), falling to the back (drawn level). Dressed sizes, metres [width, depth]; spans to checks.gd's sizing.

foundation._doc: rubble stone in lime, 18 in, 0.3 m under the pad; where it walls the cellar, down to its floor

long_joist._doc: 4x14 at 12 in (3x14 bent 1.12 of its limit under a crowd): the upper floor over the front rooms' 28 ft and the back's 22 (Kidder; L/360 at 40 lb/ft2)

tall._doc: the balloon studs run 7.9 m sill to plate (8.37 under the false front's 9.9): 4x4, as saloon B's

post._doc: 8x8 posts (the lobby's stair well), chamfered (saloon B's)

roof_joist._doc: 2x12 at 16 in: the flat roof's, front wall to the 28 ft wall to the back wall

flat_roof._doc: NEW (spec_building.gd): no trusses or rafters; the roof is a floor of its own (`floors` level 'roof') on the outer walls' plates, the front's roof ribbon (on the false front's studs) and the upper bearing partitions (full height; the others stop 2 cm short); its boards kind `board` (no crowd on them).

girders._doc: Four lines under the ground floor's joists (spans 3.0-3.4 m), on stone piers at 6 ft; in the cellar on its posts and its bearing walls. Under each partition that runs with the joists a girder of its own (saloon B's `under`), its piers left out where it is over the cellar (NEW): there the cellar's walls and posts carry it.

cellar._doc: Under the west and middle of the main block (the drawing's 0-48 ft from the west, 10 ft back to the back wall): 48 x 40 ft inside the house's foundation, rubble walls lime-washed, stone flags, 2.2 m under the girders. Its rooms are partitions on its flags: the beer cellar under the bar (kegs on stillage; the bulkhead to the lane; the trap up behind the bar; THE DRIFT out of its west wall), the stores beside it, a passage across, the coal, the ice room and the locked wine room behind. The east third is unexcavated, the floor over it on piers.
cellar._dig: NOT YET in the valley (#1220): any dug tile in the valley's first ground chunk (x -30 to 98: ValleyGround re-cuts a chunk's collision into squares round a dug tile) moves the ground under the saloon yard's card set and fails the card-game tests (saloon B's dig alone does it too). The cellar and the drift are walked in the lab (tests/test_building_hotel.gd); CellarDig digs both and covers the drift the moment this is true, once the set is inside saloon B or the re-cut leaves the squares without a tile as they were.

bulkhead._doc: The beer cellar's outside door on the saloon lane, where the brewery's dray rolls the kegs down (the undertaker's Bulkhead: a stone areaway, its steps, the passage under a lintel, slanted doors standing open).

drift._doc: NEW (Drift, src/structures/drift.gd; Sean, #1215: 'b is awesome'): the landlady's husband's keg road of 1881 to the saloon he had a share in, bricked up when he died and opened again lately by the foreman's men. A timbered drift as a mine's: sets every 4 ft (a sill on the floor, two legs, a cap), lagging boards over the caps and behind the legs, a walk of planks on the sills; through an opening under a timber lintel in the hotel's foundation and in saloon B's (`foundation.passages`). 4 ft 7 in clear under the caps (the brief's 4 ft raised so a man walks it crouched: the player crouches to 1.3 m), 3 ft between the legs. It falls toward the hotel by the two cellars' floors (`fall`). In the valley the ground over it is dug to its floor and covered over again (CellarDig: the cover flush with the lane's dirt).

ceilings._doc: Boards nailed up under the joists in every room, both floors (NEW: `levels` upper under the flat roof's joists; `holes` the stair's well, which is a gap between floors, not an opening). Plaster on lath is the next system (#1220's slice issue): these are its lath's place.

inside_finish._doc: #826's rules: the inside boards at their paint's judged width, a skirting on every boarded wall.

walls._doc: Main Street: the ground floor reads as glass (the brief's section 3): the bar's tall window and its own door at the west, the lobby's two windows either side of the main doors (a glazed pair under a fanlight), the ladies' parlour's two windows and the ladies' door at the east; above, the front rooms' low sash windows onto the gallery and the suite's French doors on the axis over the main doors. The false front's studs run to the cornice (9.9).

stairs._doc: THE GRAND STAIR (the brief's 4.1: OakStair's painted dark oak, Sean's B): one flight of 22 risers of 7 3/8 in on 10 5/8 in treads up the lobby's back wall, rising east to the upper hall; its open side railed. (The brief's two flights with a landing are one here: the builder's stairs are straight runs.)
The back stair (the servants'): 22 risers up the dining room's west wall from the back door's hall, rising to the back wall, to the upper back stair hall
the back door's steps to the yard

galleries._doc: The rails round the two wells upstairs (saloon B's gallery rail: a 36 in turned rail, square newels)

balconies._doc: THE GALLERY (Sean, #1215: an exterior balcony to be blown up later, an open railed deck): 80 x 8 ft over the walk, its deck at the upper floor (16 ft over the street), on nine 6x6 posts 10 ft apart at the walk's street edge; ONE BEAM A BAY ending on the posts (not spliced through), so a post blown out drops exactly the two bays it carries; 2x10 joists at 16 in from a ledger through the siding into the studs to the beam; a deck a bay (its boards cut at the post lines, so the fallen bays tear free); a turned-baluster rail in spans of 1.2 m. The joists hinge on the ledger and the deck tips the men down to the walk.

front._doc: The parapet over the upper windows: a frieze, the cornice on paired scroll brackets, the name board SALT CREEK HOTEL (gilt on deep red; the game's own letters). The side walls' eaves take the same cornice and brackets (`sides`), at the roof's edge.

wear._why: #901: a hotel a year old and kept: swept every morning, the lobby and the stair the most walked

materials._doc: Finishes by name from the material library (spec_building.gd finish()): a finish's `want` the moment the library has it passed at that age, until then its `use` (a passed entry). Outside, Sean's three colours (#1215, the sheet): a soft blue-grey body on narrow planed lap (`painted_bluegrey_lap`), cream trim (`painted_cream_trim`: corner boards, casings, cornice, the gallery's posts, beams and rail), a deep red on the brackets, the name board and the sash (`painted_red_trim`): each NEW, a colour of an approved paint, judged in step 4; until they pass, the approved white, buff and ox-blood. Inside: walnut wainscot in the public rooms with pale boards over (wallpaper and plaster are the next system), oak for the stair, doors and rails, the worn fir floor.

exterior._why: the soft blue-grey body (the set-direction brief, the sheet)

oak._doc: the wainscot, the well's rail, the hall stair, the doors: dark varnished wood (the library's walnut; furniture_oak drew a flat fresh orange the judges called plastic, round 1 of #867)

timber._doc: the posts, girders and the open joists over the bar: dark dressed timber (the library's walnut; R1 read as bark or concrete to the round 1 critic, oak a flat orange, planed pine a weathered grey: no dressed-timber entry yet)

red._why: the deep red picked out: brackets, the name board, the sash
